1: The Code of Warren County, Georgia, is hereby amended by adding an Article VI (Occupation Tax) in Chapter 42 (Taxation), which Article shall read as follows:
2: This Article shall be known as the Warren County Occupation Tax Ordinance.
3:
- (a) The definitions set forth in O.C.G.A. § 48-13-5 shall apply to this Article. (b) When used in this Article, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth herein:

Administrator means the County Code Enforcement Officer of such other person(s) so designated by the Board of Commissioners.

Board of Commissioners or Board means the Board of Commissioners of Warren County, Georgia.

County means Warren County, Georgia, unless the context clearly indicates otherwise.

Dominant line means the type of business within a multiple line business from which the greatest dollar amount of net income or profit is derived.

Full-time employee shall have the same meaning as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 48-13-10(a)(1), which, at the time of enactment of this Ordinance, means an employee who works 40 hours or more weekly, and that the average weekly hours of employees who work less than 40 hours weekly shall be added and such sum shall be divided by 40 to produce full-time position equivalents.

Occupation tax means the tax levied by this Article on persons doing business or engaged as practitioner of any profession or occupation in the unincorporated area of the County.

Occupation tax permit means the permit issued to a business or individual as proof of compliance with this Ordinance as set forth in Section 42-144(f) of this Article.

Ordinance means this Warren County Occupation Tax Ordinance.

Person means any natural person, sole proprietorship, partnership, corporation, limited liability company, or other legal entity.

Practitioner of any profession or occupation includes, but is not limited to, any practitioner of a profession described in O.C.G.A. § 48-13-9(c) (1) through (18) but shall not include a practitioner who is an employee of any person paying an occupation tax under this Article.

State means the State of Georgia, unless the context clearly indicates otherwise.
4:
- (a) Unless exempted or otherwise provided by state law, an occupation tax is hereby levied on:

- (1) Each business or practitioner of any profession or occupation having any location or office in any unincorporated part of the County; and

- (2) Each out-of-state business or practitioner of any profession or occupation with no location or office in the state that (a) has one or more employees or agents who exert substantial efforts within the unincorporated part of the County for the purpose of soliciting business or serving customers or client or (b) owns personal or real property which generates income and is located in the unincorporated part of the County.

- (b) The occupation tax levied by this Article is for revenue purposes only and is not for regulatory purposes, nor is the payment of the tax made a condition precedent to the practice of any such business, profession, or occupation.

- (c) The occupation tax imposed by this Article shall apply only to a business or practitioner of any profession or occupation which is subject to such a tax in accordance with Georgia law.
5:
- (a) The occupation tax is levied based on the number of employees of business or practitioner of any profession or occupation, as computed on a full-time basis or full-time position equivalent basis. An employee who works at least 40 hours weekly shall be considered a full-time position. The average weekly hours of employees who work less than 40 hours weekly shall be added and such sum shall be divided by 40 to determine the number of full-time position equivalents.

- (b) An employee who works for a business or practitioner in more than one county shall be counted as being employed in this county for the purposes of the occupation tax under this Article if the employee worked more hours in the County during the preceding year than he/she works in any other single county or municipal corporation where he/she works for the employer if the County is the local government entity in which the employee works for the longest period of time within the calendar year.

- (c) A business or practitioner with locations in more than one county and whose largest dollar volume of business or services occurs within the County, such that it is not exempt under Sec. 42-149, shall calculate its tax based on the number of employees operating within the County and as otherwise specified in subsections (a) and (b).

- (f) Upon payment of the occupation tax and administrative fee, an occupational tax permit shall be issued as certification of payment of the occupation tax and as registration of a business under this Article.

- (g) Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-13-22, when any person commences business on or after July 1 in any year, the business or occupation tax for the remaining portion of the year shall be fifty (50)

percent of the tax imposed for the entire year; provided, however, that (1) the administrative fee authorized under (e) shall not be reduced, and (2) any practitioner of a profession or occupation who elects or has elected-as his/her occupation tax the amount described in Section 42-146(a)(2) of this Article shall receive no reduction in such amount.
6: A business or practitioner with more than one type of service or product shall be classified according to its dominant service or product.
7:
- (a) In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 48-13-10(g), businesses or practitioners of professions or occupations identified in O.C.G.A. § 48-13-9(c)(2)-(18) shall elect as their occupation tax one of the following:

- (1) The occupation tax owed based on number of employees as set forth in Section 42-144 of this Article; or

- (2) An occupation tax of $200.00 for each practitioner who is licensed to provide the service, such tax to be paid at each practitioner's office or location.

- (b) This election is to be made on an annual basis and must be done by January 31st of each year. Such election shall be changed for subsequent calendar years only upon written request filed with the Board on or before February 1 of the year in which election is to be changed.
8:
In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 48-5-354, the occupation tax imposed by this Ordinance shall govern the following:

- (a) Traveling salespersons engaged in taking orders for the sale of goods when no delivery of goods is made at the time of taking the order;

- (b) A merchant or dealer, the situs of whose business is outside the taxing jurisdiction, who delivers goods previously ordered; and

- (c) The employees of a merchant or dealer who are engaged in the delivery of the goods to customers.
9:
- (a) Each person who is licensed by the Secretary of State pursuant to O.C.G.A. Title 43 shall provide evidence of proper and current state licensure to the county before the issuance of any business license under this Article.

- (b) Each person subject to any occupation tax who is also licensed by the state shall post the state license in a conspicuous place in the licensee's place of business and shall keep the license there at all times while the license remains valid.

- (c) Each business or practitioner of any profession or occupation paying the occupation tax required by this Article shall be issued an occupation tax permit per Section 42-144 of this Article and shall:

- (1) If the taxpayer maintains at least one business location or office in any unincorporated area of the County, display the current year’s permit in a conspicuous place in the taxpayer's principal place of business;

- (2) If the taxpayer does not have at least one business location or office in the unincorporated areas of the county, produce for inspection the current year’s permit upon request by the Administrator, the County Tax Commissioner, the County Sheriff, any County Deputy Sherriff, or any member of the Board.
10:
A business or practitioner of any profession or occupation shall be exempt from paying the occupation tax levied under this Article for any calendar year in which it:

- (a) Pays or owes an occupation tax to a municipal corporation or another county in this state where it does a larger dollar volume of business or performs a larger dollar volume of services.

- (b) Has paid a local business or occupation tax in another state which purports to tax the business’s or practitioner’s sales or services in this state.

The business or practitioner must provide the Administrator or its with sufficient proof that it qualifies for at least one of the exemptions set forth herein for any such exemption to be applicable.
12:
- (a) Any occupation tax owed pursuant to this Article shal] be due and payable annually within thirty (30) days following January 1. In the event that any person commences business on any date after January 1, the tax shall be due and payable thirty (30) days following the commencement of the business.

- (b) Payment of an occupational tax shall not be required prior to the commencement of business, nor shall it in any other manner act as a precondition on the practice of law or medicine within the County.

- (c) Occupation taxes that are not paid by their due date shall be delinquent. Delinquent taxes shall bear interest at the rate of 1.5 percent per month. In addition, the occupation tax, if not paid within ninety (90) days from the due date, shall have an automatic penalty of ten (10) percent of the amount of the occupation tax added.

- (d) No taxpayer shall be liable for any penalty or interest pursuant to subsection of this Article if:

- (1) The default giving rise to such penalty or interest resulted from a taxpayer's military service in the armed forces of the United States in an area designated by the President of the United States by executive order as a combat zone and was not due to gross or willful neglect or disregard of the law or of regulations or instructions issued pursuant to the law; and

- (2) The taxpayer provides proof of such military service and makes full payment of taxes due, not including penalties and interest, within sixty (60) days of such taxpayer's return from such military service.

- (e) Refund claims are subject to a three (3) year statute of limitation period and the requirements of O.C.G.A. § 48-5-380.
15:
- (a) Except in the case of judicial proceedings or other proceedings necessary to collect the occupation tax hereby levied, or as otherwise authorized or allowed by law, it shall be unlawful for any official, officer, employee, or agent of the County to divulge or make known any particulars set forth or disclosed in any occupation tax return required hereunder. Independent auditors or bookkeepers employed by the County shall be classed as "agents" of the County for the purposes of reviewing any such return hereunder. Nothing in this Section shall be construed to prohibit the publication by County officials of statistics, so classified as to prevent the identification of particular reports or returns and items thereof, or the inspection of the records by duly qualified employees of the tax departments of the State, the United States, and other local governments.

- (b) In any case, the Board, through its officers, agents, employees, or representative, may inspect the books of the business for which the returns are made, and upon demand such books or records shall be made available for inspection by the Administrator of the Board within thirty (30) days. Failure to make such books or records available within thirty (30) days shall be grounds for revocation of the tax registration currently existing to do business in the County. Adequate records shall be maintained and kept in the County for examination. If, after examination of the books or records, it is determined that a deficiency occurs as a result of underreporting, the amount of the deficiency shall be treated as a delinquent amount and shall be subject to the penalties and procedures for delinquent occupation tax amounts provided in
16: - (c) The purpose of this inspection is to enforce and determine the amount of the occupation tax contemplated in this Article, in particular: (1) confirming the eligibility of any annual exemption claimed under Sec. 42-149; (2) determining the number of full-time employees when calculating the tax under Sec. 42-144; (3) confirming the proper display and currency of any required state license; and (4) any other lawful purpose contemplated under this Article or Georgia law. The County does not conduct these inspections for any regulatory purpose.
17:
- (a) Any business required to obtain health permits, bonds, certificates of qualification, certificates of competency, or any other regulatory matter shall first, before the issuance of an occupation tax permit, show evidence that such requirements have been met.

- (b) Any business required to submit an application for continuance of the business shall do so before registration
18:
- (a) The County shall conduct at least one public hearing before adopting any ordinance or resolution regarding the occupation tax imposed in this county.

- (b) In any year when revenue from occupation taxes is greater than revenue from occupation taxes for the preceding year for a local government, the local government shall hold one or more public hearings as a part of the process of determining how to use the additional revenue.
19: This Article shall be subject to amendment or repeal, in whole or in part, at any time, and no such amendment or repeal shall be construed to deny the right of the County to assess and collect any of the taxes or other charges prescribed. Said amendment may increase or lower the amounts and tax rates of any occupation and may change the classification thereof. The payment of any occupation tax provided for shall not be construed as prohibiting the levy or collection by the jurisdiction of additional occupation taxes upon the same person, property, or business.
20: All ordinances, parts of ordinances, or regulations in conflict herewith are repealed. Where there is an apparent conflict in this Ordinance between specific and general provisions, it is the intention hereof that the specific shall control.
21: Severability. Should any section of this Ordinance be declared invalid or unconstitutional by any court of competent jurisdiction, such declaration shall not affect the validity of the Ordinance as a whole or any part thereof which is not specifically declared to be invalid or unconstitutional.
22: Codification. It is the intention of the Board of Commissioners, and it is hereby ordained that the provisions of this Ordinance shall become and be made a part of the Code of Warren County, Georgia, and the sections of this Ordinance may be renumbered to accomplish such intention.
23:
Effective Date. This Ordinance shall take effect and be in force beginning January 1, 2024, and shall continue thereafter.
